device.pinning: taskset to 4 cores of an 80-core allocation; sequential runs

method:
Collect the HIM timing benchmark (job 94496, out/main + out/repeat) into results.json and table_draft.md.

Training: train_log.csv of the unmodified training script with --log-interval 1 (samp_per_sec = 48 / epoch time).
Epochs 1-10 are warm-up, epochs 11-60 are timed. Phase A: no buffer term (as epochs 1-1000 of a real run); phase B:
buffer term on from epoch 1 (as epochs 1001-20000); with --buffer-every 2 the even epochs also advance the 64 RT
chains by one step, so B is reported per two-epoch cycle: (median even + median odd) / 2.
Sampling: bench_sample.py JSONs. Counts: exact from cond_kernels.CondNHMCResidual2Kernel / CondZ2Wrapper and
phi4_gpu.fwd_partial / rev_partial (see COUNTS below).

series.note: L16 T16 in vs_T_L16 is the native L16 model (the paper T-scan uses it); ks_L8_T16 is the separately trained K-scan model (same architecture as nat_L8_T16). prt_dT4 and prt_d4 coincide at T = 16; at T = 4 prt_d4 is the full RT (rt value repeated).

definitions.update: one transition of 4 chains held in one batched tensor (longchain.py step loop); s/update is the median over 200 timed updates after 20 warm-up updates
definitions.forward_path: PhiStepper.start = base draw + T forward stages + action; s per path at batch 1024 (SNIS / pre-generated path-IMH proposals) and at batch 4
definitions.prt_d_T4: pRT with return depth d = T/4 (s = 3T/4)
definitions.prt_d4: pRT with fixed return depth d = 4 (s = T - 4); at T = 16 both are s = 12 (paper); at T = 4, d = 4 is the full RT
definitions.train_epoch: s per epoch, batch 48, median of epochs 11-60; A = before the buffer term (epochs 1-1000 of a run), B = buffer phase per two-epoch cycle (epochs 1001-20000)

training_logs_note.caveat: devices differ (iqcb: shared L40S GPU; HIM: CPU, 4 or 16 threads); samp_per_sec is logged at epochs that are multiples of 200, which are even epochs and therefore always include the buffer RT step: the sum over segments overestimates the buffer phase; eval_log wall_sec is the wall time since the last (re)start
